en-2483.en: Did you run? Did you jump?

en-2484.en: I rode a bike in the park, in the park, in the park.

en-2485.en: And ouch, I hurt my foot!

en-2486.en: Now I am taller, taller than before.

en-2487.en: Every day I grow bigger. Every day I grow more.

en-2488.en: Once I was a young boy, younger than I am today.

en-2489.en: Now I am a big boy, and I’m bigger every day.

en-2490.en: For school I got up early, earlier than before.

en-2491.en: Every day I get up early, sometimes at four!

en-2492.en: But now I talk more than before. I always talk with joy!

en-2494.en: Your feet are bigger than mine.

en-2507.en: Tell us about your school, please.

en-2512.en: Life is what you make it.

en-2514.en: Pete: Can I please buy your straw?

en-2516.en: Pete: I am going to build a house with it.

en-2518.en: Pete: That’s OK. I need a house before winter.

en-2519.en: Pat: Can I please buy your sticks?

en-2521.en: Pat: I am going to build a house with them.

en-2523.en: Pat: That’s OK. I need a house before winter.

en-2524.en: Paul: Can I please buy your bricks?

en-2526.en: Paul: I am going to build a house with them.

en-2527.en: Brick-seller: Great! Bricks are very strong.

en-2529.en: Paul: Bricks are heavier than straw and sticks.

en-2530.en: Brick houses are stronger than straw houses and stick houses.

en-2531.en: Narrator: The man sold Paul the bricks. Paul built his house of bricks.

en-2532.en: Pat built his house of sticks. Pete built his house of straw.

en-2533.en: Wolf: Little Pig, Little Pig, let me in!

en-2534.en: Pete: No way! No way! Not by the hair on my chin.

en-2535.en: Wolf: Then I will blow your house down.

en-2536.en: Pete & Pat: No way! No way! Not by the hair on my chin.

en-2537.en: Pete, Pat & Paul: No way! No way! Not by the hair on my chin.

en-2542.en: Little Red-Cap: Yes, Mum. I will be careful.

en-2543.en: Narrator: She went into the woods. She saw a wolf.

en-2547.en: Wolf: What do you have there?

en-2548.en: Little Red-Cap: I have some cake and medicine for my grandmother.

en-2549.en: Wolf: Where does your grandmother live?

en-2550.en: Little Red-Cap: Her house is far. She lives near the mountain.

en-2551.en: Wolf: Listen, Little Red-Cap. Can you hear the sweet little birds?

en-2552.en: They are singing. And look! How pretty the flowers are!

en-2553.en: Why don’t you take some flowers to your grandmother?

en-2555.en: Narrator: Little Red-Cap picked some flowers for her grandmother.

en-2557.en: Grandmother: I’m in bed. Come in.

en-2559.en: Grandmother: What a strange voice you have, Little Red-Cap.

en-2560.en: Wolf: I have a cold. My throat is sore.

en-2564.en: Little Red-Cap: What a strange voice you have, Grandmother!

en-2565.en: Little Red-Cap: What big eyes you have, Grandmother!

en-2566.en: Wolf: They help me see you better.

en-2567.en: Little Red-Cap: What big ears you have, Grandmother!

en-2568.en: Wolf: They help me hear you better.

en-2569.en: Little Red-Cap: What large hands you have, Grandmother!

en-2570.en: Wolf: They help me hug you better.

en-2571.en: Little Red-Cap: What big teeth you have, Grandmother!

en-2572.en: Wolf: They help me eat you better.

en-2573.en: Narrator: The wolf jumped out of the bed. He ate Little Red-Cap.

en-2574.en: Grandmother: Thank you for helping us!
